title: Site Reliability Engineer
summary: Site Reliability Engineers use software engineering to keep services fast and available: they set reliability targets, build monitoring, automate repetitive work and lead the response when things break. It suits students who enjoy both coding and debugging systems.

sources.title: Site Reliability Engineering books (free to read online) – Google SRE
Site Reliability Engineering: table of contents – Google SRE
DevOps Roadmap: Learn to become a DevOps Engineer or SRE – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: Linux and operating-system basics
nodes.summary: SREs debug live machines. Get comfortable with the shell, processes, memory, disks, file systems, permissions and logs, and know which command to reach for when a server is slow.

resources.title: Introduction to Linux (LFS101) – The Linux Foundation
The Missing Semester of Your CS Education – MIT

nodes.proof: Write a short troubleshooting guide for a Linux VM: how you found the process using the most CPU, a full disk, and a crashed service.

nodes.title: Programming and Git
nodes.summary: Google describes SRE as software engineers doing operations work, so coding matters. Learn one language well (Python is a friendly start), plus data structures basics and Git.
nodes.proof: A Python tool in a public repo that parses a log file and reports error counts and slowest requests.

nodes.title: Networking fundamentals
nodes.summary: Many incidents come down to DNS, TCP, load balancers or HTTP errors. Learn the TCP/IP layers, DNS, routing and HTTP well enough to trace a request end to end.

resources.title: Computer Networks and Internet Protocol – NPTEL (IIT Kharagpur)

nodes.proof: Diagram and explain how a request travels from a browser to your app, and which tool you would use to check each hop.

nodes.title: Containers, Kubernetes and one cloud
nodes.summary: Modern services run in containers on cloud platforms. Learn Docker, Kubernetes basics (deployments, services, scaling, rollouts) and the core services of one cloud provider.
nodes.proof: Run a containerised app on a local minikube cluster with three replicas and do a rolling update.

nodes.title: SLIs, SLOs and error budgets
nodes.summary: This is what makes SRE different. Learn to pick indicators users care about (SLIs), set targets (SLOs), and use the error budget to decide when to ship features and when to fix reliability.

resources.title: Implementing SLOs – The Site Reliability Workbook
Part II: Principles (Embracing Risk, Service Level Objectives) – SRE book

nodes.proof: Write a one-page SLO document for a sample app: two SLIs, their targets, the time window and what happens when the budget runs out.

sources.title: Implementing SLOs – The Site Reliability Workbook

nodes.title: Monitoring and observability
nodes.summary: Start with the four golden signals: latency, traffic, errors and saturation. Then learn to collect metrics with Prometheus, build Grafana dashboards, and add traces and logs with OpenTelemetry.

resources.title: Monitoring Distributed Systems – SRE book, Chapter 6

nodes.proof: A Grafana dashboard for your app showing all four golden signals, fed by Prometheus.

sources.title: Monitoring Distributed Systems – SRE book, Chapter 6

nodes.title: Incident response, postmortems and toil
nodes.summary: Learn how teams run on-call, manage an incident with clear roles, and write blameless postmortems. Learn to spot toil (repetitive manual work) and remove or automate it.

resources.title: Postmortem Culture: Learning from Failure – Google SRE
Eliminating Toil – The Site Reliability Workbook

nodes.proof: A blameless postmortem for a real failure from your own projects: timeline, impact, root cause and action items.

sources.title: Incident Response – The Site Reliability Workbook

nodes.title: Project: run a service with an SLO
nodes.summary: Deploy a small web service, define its SLO, build dashboards and alerts on the SLO, then break it on purpose (kill a pod, add latency) and write the postmortem.

resources.title: Get started with Grafana and Prometheus – Grafana Docs

nodes.proof: A public repo with the SLO document, dashboard screenshots, an alert rule that fired during your test, and the postmortem.

sources.title: Implementing SLOs – The Site Reliability Workbook

nodes.title: Interview preparation and job search
nodes.summary: SRE interviews usually mix coding, Linux and networking troubleshooting, system design and reliability concepts. Fresher SRE openings are few; many people start in DevOps, backend or support roles and move across.

resources.title: The Site Reliability Workbook: table of contents – Google SRE

nodes.proof: Do three mock interviews: one coding, one 'the site is slow, debug it' scenario, and one walkthrough of your SLO project.
